defect.description: A NETRC path is still expanded under the home directory: os.path.expanduser(f"~/{name}") turns NETRC=/etc/ci/netrc into a path like /home/user//etc/ci/netrc, so a NETRC file outside the home directory (an absolute path, or one starting with ~) is never found and no credentials are returned; only the default NETRC_FILES names should get the ~/ prefix.

review_items: NETRC env var path incorrectly prefixed with ~/ via expanduser, so absolute paths are never found and None is returned; the test only covers a bare filename
votes.evidence_quote: This always prepends `~/` to every location. When `NETRC` is set to an absolute path like `/etc/secrets/.netrc` (the common pattern), it resolves to `~/etc/secrets/.netrc` — a path that won't exist, so the function silently returns `None`.
votes.justification: The review points to the expanduser(f"~/{name}") call in get_netrc_auth. It explains that this prefixes an absolute NETRC path with the home directory, so no file is found and no credentials are returned. That is the known defect, and the proposed fix matches it.
